base: a fresh git clone of the project at HEAD b64562a, outside the project; the working tree differs from HEAD only in decisions/README.md and the new audit files (git status), no code

findings.check: oversized files and functions; recorded decision decisions/0005 D10 (pure modules plus a thin DOM layer)
findings.title: The page's DOM layer is one 3307-line closure: app.js is 3551 lines, 5 to 10 times its neighbours
findings.evidence: node <outside the project>/fnsize.mjs src/pixel-office/public/app.js -> '3552 lines; 129 functions; largest: createApp@245=3307, decorate@3351=156, mainCardTree@2293=153, renderJournal@1188=128'. wc -l of the neighbouring page modules: office-view.js 690, model.js 585, panels.js 528, the rest 200-400 (texts.js 1081 is data). decisions/0005-pixel-office-design.md:68 D10 chose 'pure ES modules without DOM ... plus a thin DOM layer'. The pure logic does live in the other modules (app.js imports buildModel, buildOffice, journalRows, buildHistory and others), so the split itself holds; the DOM layer is not thin. One closure holds about 40 mutable state variables (app.js:263-300) shared by about 120 inner functions; its test file test/pixel-office-page.test.js is 6090 lines, the largest in the project.
findings.recommendation: Split createApp by screen area (header and 'Сейчас', office and card, journal, task panel, guide wiring) into modules that take the shared state object explicitly, following the pattern already used by guide.js, tour.js and hints.js; no change of behaviour, the existing page tests as the guard. If ORCH reads D10 as violated, this is a divergence from a recorded decision (High) - see result.issues I1.

findings.check: the list of addresses and methods matches tools/README.md and docs/design/REQ-001-pixel-office.md
findings.title: The Pixel Office design still says POST /api/events is the only write path; the code and README have a second one, POST /api/note
findings.evidence: grep -n 'единственный путь записи' docs/design/REQ-001-pixel-office.md -> 185 and 2833 ('| `POST /api/events` | **единственный путь записи** |'); grep -n 'api/note' docs/design/REQ-001-pixel-office.md -> nothing; grep -ln 'api/note' docs/design/*.md -> only REQ-008-history.md. server.js:453 routes POST /api/note; tools/README.md:200 and :209 describe two write paths. Live probe on a separate server (port 0, own state folder outside the project): 'POST /api/note -> 200 {"request_time":null,"request_time_auto":false}'.
findings.recommendation: Add to REQ-001 design section 5.2 (and the picture at :185 and item 3 at :3046) the second write path with a reference to the REQ-008 design, or a note at the top of section 5 that REQ-008 changed it.

findings.check: one mechanism in neighbouring places: append-only journals and all-or-nothing writes
findings.title: The Pixel Office journal appends without fsync and without rollback; the neighbouring Team journal does both
findings.evidence: grep -n 'fsync\|flush' src/pixel-office/*.js -> nothing. team/journal.js:150-153: 'On a failed write or fsync the file is cut back to expectedBytes (ftruncate + fsync), so either all the lines are written or the journal is as it was.' pixel-office/journal.js:62-65: a cut-off tail becomes 'a separate corrupt line' at the next append. The REQ-001 design accepts this (design line 687, the append contract), so it is not a divergence; but after a failed partial append the server answers 500 while a fragment stays in the journal for good and is reported as a corrupt line on reads.
findings.recommendation: Either give the Pixel Office append the Team rollback (ftruncate to the size before the write, on failure) or record in the REQ-001 design why the two journals differ, so the next reader does not 'fix' one by the other.

findings.check: error responses are of one kind (Q10); one mechanism in neighbouring places: the three HTTP servers
findings.title: Three HTTP servers copy the same base by hand, and it has drifted: Pixel Office answers 403 and 405 with an empty body, the team page and the picker answer with JSON and a text
findings.where: tools/src/pixel-office/server.js:86-114, :438, :450-461; tools/src/web/server.js:107-129, :287-293; tools/src/picker/server.js:155-170. Also parts team and picker.
findings.evidence: Live probe on the separate Pixel Office server: 'DELETE /api/events -> 405 - ' (no Content-Type, empty body), 'GET / [host=evil.example] -> 403 - ', while every other error is JSON ('404 {"error":"not_found"}', '401 {"error":"unauthorized"}', '400 {"error":"time_skew"}', '413 {"error":"too_large"}', '500 {"error":"write_failed"}'). web/server.js:291 refuses 405 with failure(405, TEXT.badRequest) - a JSON body with a text. commonHeaders() is byte-identical in pixel-office/server.js:86 and web/server.js:107; the 413 drain is written three ways (pixel-office answerTooLarge with socket.setTimeout, web discard(), picker discard()). The empty 403 is what the REQ-001 design asks for (design line 2813), so this is a drift between neighbours, not a divergence from the design.
findings.recommendation: Agree one error body for all three servers (code plus text) and move the shared base (headers, JSON answer, 413 drain, Host check) into one module, or keep the copies and add one parity test over the three servers.

findings.title: HISTORY_SERVICE is exported by the page texts and used only by a test
findings.evidence: grep -rn HISTORY_SERVICE src test -> only texts.js:462 (definition) and test/pixel-office-panels.test.js:1266. The page shows the same words through texts.js:76 and :199.
findings.recommendation: Remove the constant and let the test take the text from the place the page uses, or use the constant in the page.

findings.check: one mechanism in neighbouring places (AP-014): shared helpers
findings.title: team/common.js exports has and isPlainObject, but store.js, schema.js and engine/channel.js keep their own copies; lstatOrNull is copied four times in team
findings.where: tools/src/team/common.js:4, :10; copies in tools/src/team/store.js:60, :66, :102; tools/src/team/schema.js:397, :407; tools/src/team/engine/channel.js:132, :149; tools/src/team/files.js:32; tools/src/team/home.js:99
findings.evidence: grep -rn -E '^(export )?function isPlainObject' src -> 7 definitions, 4 of them in team (common.js exported, store.js, schema.js, channel.js private). grep -rln 'from "./common.js"' -> only executor.js, executors/scripted.js and one more use the shared helper. The four team copies of lstatOrNull are line-for-line the same (store.js:102-109, files.js:32-39, home.js:99-106, channel.js:132-139). The copies agree today, so nothing is broken; a change of the rule in common.js would reach two places out of six.
findings.recommendation: Make store.js, schema.js and engine/channel.js import has and isPlainObject from common.js, and move lstatOrNull into common.js for the four team files.

findings.check: one mechanism in neighbouring places (AP-014): accepting result files
findings.title: A result file with a bad name refuses the attempt in runner.js but is silently dropped in engine/single-run.js
findings.evidence: single-run.js:163 'if (!checkResultName(name).ok) continue;' - the file is skipped and the run is still recorded as ok with fewer names; runner.js:616/:622 'if (!checkResultName(name).ok) return fileRefusal();' - the attempt fails with the reason «файл с результатом не удалось принять». runner.js also checks every file before the first write (step 1, :605-625); single-run.js writes as it goes (:159-171). The REQ-013 design does not mention importOutputs (grep -> nothing). The path is used by runs without a task with the scripted executor (single-run.js:156-158).
findings.recommendation: Use one acceptance helper for both places (check all names first, refuse on a bad one), or record in the REQ-013 design why a run without a task may drop a file, and say so in its result.

findings.check: part boundaries: modules do not import each other in a circle; oversized functions
findings.title: executor.js and the two executors import each other in a circle
findings.evidence: node <outside the project>/graph.mjs (import graph of src/) -> 'CYCLES 2: src/team/executor.js -> src/team/executors/claude-cli.js; src/team/executor.js -> src/team/executors/scripted.js'. executor.js:7 says 'Everything here is pure except getExecutor, which imports the two executors'; the REQ-010 design (line 105) places getExecutor there. It works with ES modules today because the executors use the imported names only at call time.
findings.recommendation: Move getExecutor into its own small module (for example team/executors/index.js) so executor.js stays the pure interface and the cycle disappears.

findings.title: Two very long functions in team: createEngine 944 lines and runTask 532 lines
findings.where: tools/src/team/engine/engine.js:107 (createEngine); tools/src/team/runner.js:157 (runTask, with the inner attempts 189 lines at :303)
findings.evidence: node <outside the project>/fnsize.mjs -> 'engine.js 1087 lines; largest: createEngine@107=944', 'runner.js 705 lines; largest: runTask@157=532, attempts@303=189'. Neighbours: reducer.js largest function 49 lines, schema.js 70, store.js 107. A reader of one step of the engine has to hold the whole closure state; the engine's tests are spread over 18 files.

findings.evidence: grep -rn OUTCOMES src test -> executor.js:19 (definition, no reader), scripted.js:28 and :105 (own list of 5 of the 7 values). The REQ-010 design lists OUTCOMES among the exports of executor.js (line 824).

findings.title: lookOfView, ownLookOfView and deskForQuestion are not called by any code
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'lookOfView\|ownLookOfView\|deskForQuestion' src test -> lookOfView and ownLookOfView: only the definitions; deskForQuestion: the definition and test/picker-look.test.js (LK-6d). size_view.method: wc -l of JS under each part's folders (pages separately), CSS/HTML separately, JSON data separately; tests by file name prefix in tools/test (159 files); fixtures by folder

claude.note: 37 role files and settings.json; no code

size_view.is_it_justified: Mostly yes. About 50 000 lines of code in tools/src, of which 4 877 are picker demo data and 5 000 are CSS; tests are 2 to 2.6 times the code in tools-core, pixel-office and team, which matches the bar's demand of a test per criterion and failure tests with a state check. Not justified: the Pixel Office page DOM layer as one 3307-line closure (ARC-01), the picker fixtures as near-identical full copies (ARC-14), and the long closures of the team engine and runner (ARC-09). The servers' createX closures (300-390 lines) are the same pattern in all three and are acceptable.
